newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Thursday and traders said the rises were mainly due to listing of two new domestic A share firms today, which attracted funds from the repo market.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.18 percent from 7.50 percent last Friday. The market was closed from Saturday to Wednesday for the National Day holiday.
Turnover surged to 13.03 million lots from 4.95 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
A share firms Worldbest Enterprise Development Co and Xiamen International Trading (Group) Co made debut in Shanghai today.
Traders expect the rates to fall on Friday after fever on the two new A shares calms down.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on weak market sentiment with investors expecting coupons for new T-bills and T-bonds to drop due to falling inflation.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 closed down at 120.23 yuan from 120.91 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 840,526 lots from 2.78 million.
Traders expect the downtrend to continue in the short term.
